investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota or physical VM slot limit was reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 131–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing all required contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota or physical VM slot limit was reached), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 131–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing all required contract assertions (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-28T21:25–21:27Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pods: only 2 nodes carry that resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval never reached the agent creation step, so no runtime evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by an underlying Kubernetes cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" and the pod remained unscheduled for 147 seconds before the eval timed out. Because the agent pod never started, the probe returned no evidence, causing a complete contract gap across all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-state all reporting the same scheduler reason.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any VM slot contention. If the selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, this could explain why capacity appears insufficient even at low load.

TERTIARY — eval cleanup not releasing VM slots between sequential checks: if a prior eval run's remote agent pods were not fully cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916), leaked pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, preventing new scheduling. No cleanup failure evidence is present in the packet, so this remains speculative.
LOWER — transient cluster event (node drain, maintenance, or scale-down) temporarily reducing the 2 kata-capable nodes below their normal VM capacity. No node event evidence is present in the packet.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity on the 2 eligible nodes to determine whether slots are exhausted by concurrent workloads or leaked eval pods.
List all pods in the eval namespace currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations and terminate any that are orphaned from prior probe runs to free capacity.
Verify that the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is correctly terminating remote agent pods after each eval run, and add cleanup verification logging if it is not.
Audit the node affinity/selector configuration for remote agent pods to confirm that 4 of 6 nodes being excluded is intentional; if not, correct the labels or selector to expand the schedulable pool.

Consider provisioning additional kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on existing eligible nodes or adding new kata-capable nodes if the current 2-node pool is insufficient for concurrent eval and production workloads.
Monitor the next scheduled eval run to determine if the failure recurs; if it does, escalate to the infrastructure team responsible for the Kubernetes cluster and kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool.

If a re-run of the eval immediately succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief node pressure event) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 nodes that failed affinity/selector are confirmed to have been intentionally excluded and the 2 eligible nodes have never had more than 2 VM slots, the issue is a capacity sizing problem rather than exhaustion from concurrent load.

If pod cleanup logs show that withCleanup successfully terminated all prior remote agent pods before this run, the leaked-pod hypothesis is disproved and the cause is purely concurrent external workload or insufficient provisioned capacity.
If the remote-agent-create sibling check had passed (it did not), that would suggest the failure is isolated to the runtime check rather than a cluster-wide scheduling constraint.

Add a cleanup-verification eval step that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods remain in the eval namespace before each remote-agents probe run, catching VM slot leaks proactively.
Add a node-affinity health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's affinity/selector, alerting if the schedulable pool drops below a configured minimum.

Consider a dedicated eval that measures kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability as a standalone infrastructure health check, decoupled from the end-to-end remote-agent-create flow, so capacity exhaustion is visible before it causes agent creation timeouts.
